title: The Atacama Pathfinder Experiment (APEX)
caption: The Atacama Pathfinder Experiment under the Milky Way, Chajnantor plateau
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: The Atacama Pathfinder Experiment, or APEX, stands on the Chajnantor plateau, 5000 metres up in the Chilean Andes. Above it, the plane of our galaxy, the Milky Way, stretches across the sky, resembling a band of faint, glowing clouds.
The central region of the Milky Way lies to the left of APEX. According to the source, that is where a supermassive black hole sits at the core of our galaxy.

APEX is run jointly by the Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy, the Onsala Space Observatory and ESO, and ESO is responsible for operating it at Chajnantor. The photograph was taken by Babak Tafreshi for The World At Night. The glow of the Milky Way is the combined light of vast numbers of stars, too distant to pick out one by one.

understand.summary: This is a night landscape photograph by Babak Tafreshi. The source gives no camera or colour details.
understand.eye: A camera exposure gathers far more light than the eye, so the Milky Way's glowing clouds appear brighter than they would to someone on the plateau.
